deed: טבל אירובוטיקס קוטפת פרי ברחפנים אוטונומיים ופותרת מחסור בקוטפים
title: Yaniv Maor and Tevel built flying robots that pick fruit in orchards that lack pickers

trailer.text: Yaniv Maor is a computer engineer and tech executive with experience in machine vision, and he is the founder and CEO of Tevel.
Tevel is an Israeli startup from Tel Nof in central Israel that has developed flying autonomous robots for picking fruit.
According to AgFunder News, engineer Yaniv Maor founded it in 2016 to solve the labor shortage in fruit farming.
The robots take off from a base station, and with a mechanical arm they pick fruits from the trees one by one and place them in a bin on the ground.
According to the Jewish Chronicle, the robots operate today in Italy, Chile, the US and Israel.
Maor said that Tevel is not a substitute for human labor but a solution to the labor shortage.

glance.label: Collaborations
glance.value: About 20 in the US and Europe, according to ISRAEL21c

paragraphs.text: According to the World Bank, only about one percent of all workers in Israel are employed in agriculture.

According to Future Farming, which relies on Jewish Business News, Maor watched a television report in which young Israelis were offered a considerable sum of money to work in orchards, and none of them lasted even a full day.

According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, the relative number of orchard workers may have halved over the past two decades, and over the same period fruit production doubled.
According to Maor, the gap between growing fruit consumption and shrinking farming manpower is widening in the US, China, Japan and Europe.
According to ISRAEL21c, in the US most pickers were workers from Mexico, and they did not return after the pandemic.
According to the World Economic Forum, COVID travel restrictions prevented seasonal workers from crossing borders.
As a result, much of the fruit is left hanging on the trees, because there are not enough people to pick it when it is ripe.
According to ISRAEL21c, more than 10% of the world's fruit is not harvested today.
According to the same source, fruit rotting on the trees or on the ground costs growers about $30 billion in sales each year.

stations.title: A documentary, a patent and a new company

paragraphs.text: In an interview from August 2022, Maor said that about ten years earlier he had watched a television documentary about the labor crisis in agriculture in Israel.
According to ISRAEL21c, he is not a farmer by trade but a tech executive with experience in machine vision and electro-optics.
Maor said he studied computer engineering and systems engineering at the Technion.
Maor said that in the past, processing power and algorithms were not strong enough to build a picking robot.
According to him, he thought of flying robots, wrote a patent, and so the company's journey began.
According to Future Farming, the company is named after Maor's daughter.
Maor founded the company together with Oz Desheh.
Maor said that Oz Desheh died of cancer in the company's early days.
His brother, Eyal Desheh, joined the company after Oz's death in October 2017.

stations.title: How a flying robot picks an apple

paragraphs.text: Tevel says it has developed an automated flying machine that does the hard work of picking quickly and efficiently.
The robots take off from a base station.
According to the Jewish Chronicle, several robots are tethered by cable to a mobile platform.
According to the Jewish Chronicle, the robot hovers next to the tree and picks the fruit with a gentle twist of suction arms.
According to Calcalist, the mechanical arm is one meter long.
The machine takes the fruits one by one and places them in a bin on the ground.
According to Maor, the machine combines artificial intelligence vision, balancing, maneuvering and perception algorithms, mechanical components, sensors and a strong processor.
According to him, the drone is fully autonomous, and an operator is needed only for inspection.
According to the Times of Israel article, the prototype can identify oranges and many varieties of apples.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the drone can also thin and prune in apple and orange orchards.

stations.title: Five weeks in an orchard in Italy

paragraphs.text: The company conducted its first commercial field trials in an apple orchard in Italy.
Maor said that in the trial the robots worked non-stop for five weeks and picked fruit.
Maor said that by the middle of the pilot the robots became even better than the human pickers.
According to him, in selective picking the robot was better and more consistent than the pickers, with a difference of more than 10% in grading.
According to Maor, in Italy the robots picked as well as or better than the human pickers.

stations.title: From apples to peaches, from Italy to California

paragraphs.text: Tevel started with apples, and has since added peaches, nectarines, plums and apricots.
According to the Tevel website, the robots are changing harvesting practices in orchards in Italy, the US, Chile and Israel.
According to ISRAEL21c, the company has about 20 collaborations in the US and Europe, including in Italy and California.
According to Calcalist, most of Tevel's orders come from customers in North America and Europe, and there are also orders from China, Japan, South Korea and Brazil.
Maor said that in that year Tevel had about 20 robots, and that hundreds of units were planned for the following year.
According to ISRAEL21c, setup takes one to two hours, and Tevel personnel stay for a week to train the farmer.
Tevel charges the farmer a service fee that includes all the costs.
Maor estimates that one robot can cover one hectare over a harvesting season.
According to the Times of Israel article, the company wants to be a service company that sets up joint ventures with local growers.
John White, CEO of Marom Orchards, was among the first farmers to use the robots.
He said that reliable pickers are needed, and that they must be paid wages and have visas, housing and food arranged for them.
Maor said that the main reason for using the robots is not the savings but the fact that people are simply not available.

stations.title: The people, the money and the recognition

paragraphs.text: The company is led by founder and CEO Yaniv Maor and chairman Eyal Desheh.
Desheh was formerly chairman of Isracard and CFO of Teva and of Check Point.
At the time of the reported funding round, two Israeli funds, Maverick Ventures and OurCrowd, together held 27% of Tevel's shares.
According to AgFunder News, the investors in the $20 million round included Kubota and AgFunder.
According to the World Economic Forum, Tevel, an Israeli company, invented a flying autonomous robot that identifies and picks fruit using artificial intelligence.
According to The Robot Report, in 2020 Tevel demonstrated fruit picking with a tethered drone using vision and AI.
According to the Tevel website, the company has won awards and recognition in agriculture and robotics.
Maor said that the company's vision is to transform fruit picking from traditional manual work into a technological process.
Maor foresees that in the future fewer people will work in picking, and more will work in managing the robots, analyzing the data and making decisions.
According to the Jewish Chronicle, the robots are still slower than human pickers.
According to the same source, they pick about a ton, half of what a person picks.
According to Calcalist, the drones then worked only in daylight, and the company was working on night vision.
According to DroneXL, as automation advances, questions arise about job losses.
According to the World Economic Forum, Tevel stresses that the robots are designed to complement human pickers, not to replace them.
Maor said that Tevel is a solution to the labor shortage and not a substitute for human labor.
Tevel hoped to commercialize its first drones in 2020.
According to the Jerusalem Post, the company hoped to bring a patented fleet of drones to market by 2020.

claims.text: מאור אמר שחזון החברה הוא להפוך את קטיף הפירות מפרקטיקה ידנית מסורתית לתהליך טכנולוגי מתקדם.
claims.quote: Our vision is to transform fruit harvesting from the traditional manual practice to an advanced technological process.

claims.text: מאור צופה שבעתיד פחות אנשים יעבדו בקטיף ויותר יעבדו בניהול הרובוטים, ניתוח הנתונים וקבלת החלטות.
claims.quote: In the future fewer people will work in picking and more will work managing the robots, analysing the data and making decisions.

claims.text: לפי ה-Jewish Chronicle, הרובוטים עדיין איטיים מהקוטפים האנושיים ומסוגלים לקטוף כטון, חצי ממה שאדם קוטף.
claims.quote: The Tevel robots aren’t yet as fast as human pickers. They can currently manage about a ton, half as much as a person.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, הרחפנים פועלים כרגע רק באור יום, והחברה עובדת על הוספת יכולות ראיית לילה.
claims.quote: The drones are currently only operational in daylight, but the company is working to give the drone night-vision capabilities to increase productivity.

claims.text: לפי DroneXL, ככל שהאוטומציה מתקדמת עולות שאלות לגבי עקירת מקומות עבודה.
claims.quote: Yet, as automation advances, questions linger about job displacement.

claims.text: לפי הפורום הכלכלי העולמי, טבל מדגישה שהרובוטים נועדו להשלים קוטפים אנושיים ולא להחליף אותם.
claims.quote: Tevel insists its robots are designed to complement human fruit pickers rather than replace them.

claims.text: טבל קיוותה למסחר את הרחפנים הראשונים שלה ב-2020.
claims.quote: Tevel hopes to commercialize its first drones in 2020.

claims.text: לפי הג'רוזלם פוסט, טבל עובדת על צי רחפנים מוגן בפטנט שהיא מקווה שיגיע לשוק עד 2020.
claims.quote: It is working on a patented fleet of drones, which it hopes will hit the market by 2020.

claims.text: לפי טיימס אוף ישראל, טבל נוסדה באוגוסט 2016 ומעסיקה כ-15 אנשים.
claims.quote: Tevel Aerobotics Technologies was founded in August 2016 and employs around 15 people.

claims.text: לפי Farmers Journal, החברה הישראלית נוסדה ב-2017 וגייסה לאחרונה 20 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: The Israeli-based agtech company was founded in 2017 and recently secured $20m in investor funding.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, מצבת העובדים בטבל עומדת כיום על 56 ומתרחבת.
claims.quote: Staffing count is currently 56 and growing. The company’s chairman of the board is Eyal Desheh

claims.text: לפי הכתבה, טבל סיימה סבב גיוס שני וגייסה כ-10 מיליון דולר בעזרת משקיעים מלאכים.
claims.quote: The company has just concluded its second round of investment, raising around $10 million thanks to the support of angel investors

claims.text: לפי נתוני Pitchbook שצוטטו באלגמיינר, הגיוס של טבל עד כה עמד על 10 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: Funding to date: $10 million, according to Pitchbook data

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, המערכת בפיתוח כחמש שנים והחברה גייסה כ-30 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: the system has been in development for some five years and the company has raised around $30 million.

claims.text: מאור סיפר שהחברה גייסה בסך הכול למעלה מ-30 מיליון דולר.
claims.quote: With funding, we’ve raised over $30 million overall, and this year in Q1, we will start a new investment round

claims.text: לדברי מאור, שוק הקטיף העולמי מסתכם בכ-500 מיליארד דולר בשנה.
claims.quote: The worldwide market for fruit picking amounts to some $500 billion per year, he said.

claims.text: לפי כלכליסט, החברה טוענת לפוטנציאל של 3 מיליארד דולר מכירות שנתיות במכירה למגדלים בארה"ב ובאירופה ועוד 30 מיליארד דולר בשאר העולם.
claims.quote: The company claims it has a potential for $3 billion in annual sales to growers in the U.S. and Europe and an additional $30 billion in the rest of the world.

claims.text: לפי ישראל21c, הרובוטים של טבל יכולים לעבוד 24/7 בזמן הקציר.
claims.quote: Tevel’s robotic pickers can work 24/7 during the harvest

claims.text: לפי Future Farming, כל פלטפורמה אוטונומית משמשת מרכז לעד 6 רחפני קטיף.
claims.quote: autonomous platforms that each serve as a hub for up to 6 harvesting drones

claims.text: לפי Farmers Journal, כל רכב מצויד בשישה רובוטים מעופפים.
claims.quote: Each vehicle is equipped with six flying robots.
